newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia may slow car tariff cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia may slow car tariff cuts - paper.

text.p: Australia would slow the pace of cuts to car tariffs under a plan being discussed by national government departments, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The plan would see tariffs cut from 15 percent in 2000 to five percent by 2010, instead of by 2004 as proposed by the government's Productivity Commission.
The commission's recommendations, in a recent draft report, have prompted warnings from car makers that they could pull out of Australia.
General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co both have large manufacturing and assembly operations in Australia.

The Treasury and the Department of Industry, Science and Technology, discussing future protection for the industry, have also raised the possibility of ending an export facilitation scheme, replacing it with productivity-linked bounties, the paper said.
The government has yet to decide its formal response to the commission's recommendations.
A final commission report is due in May, after industry consultations.
